{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=critical+evaluation+of+automated+reasoning+tree+expansion+methods+as+epistemic+self-correction+versus+blind+search+optimization&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1023/a:1006303512524\", \"title\": [\"Resolution versus Search: Two Strategies for SAT\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1023/a:1006303512524\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2000, 2]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1023/a:1006350622830\", \"title\": [\"Local Search Algorithms for SAT: An Empirical Evaluation\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1023/a:1006350622830\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2000, 5]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.5977016\", \"title\": [\"Epistemic Consistency as an Optimization Target for AI Systems v1.1 A Conceptual Architecture for Structured Self-Correction\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5977016\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1093/med/9780190912925.003.0007\", \"title\": [\"Variability Versus Diversity in Variety\"], \"abstract\": \"

Making sense of the enormous variety of patient phenomena creates the epistemic conundrum. Is each and every patient taken as a unique entity, or is there an economical set of principles and facts from which each and every patient can be reconstructed? Empiric medicine favors the former, risking Solipsism of the Present Moment. Rationalist/allopathic medicine favors the latter but makes application of knowledge to the individual patient problematic. The conundrum cannot be resolved by simply taking the “average” of all patients or some other measure of central tendency. While it is possible to find the average weight of animals in Dundas, Ontario, it would have little meaning, except perhaps in exceptional circumstance. A central question in statistics is whether the mean (average) reflects the true nature of the phenomenon or does its range (variance)? Assuming the former is greatly enabling in medical decision-making and research but may be misleading.

However, its implementation remain uneven when regulatory design is not matched by operational capacity, territorial accessibility, reliable data, and realistic circularity outcomes. This article examines this issue through the Brazilian reverse logistics system for household medicine waste. Drawing on documentary analysis of legal frameworks and LogMed/SINIR implementation reports for 2021–2023, combined with eleven semi-structured interviews with pharmacies, pharmaceutical manufactures, and a sectoral entity, the study investigates how shared responsibility shapes implementation in practice. The findings show that the system expanded in the municipalities covered, the number of collection points, and the collected volume, but expansion did not achieve full infrastructure density or balanced implementation. Pharmacies and drugstores operate as frontline nodes and bear significant operational burdens, including space constraints, consumer disposal errors, segregation requirements, and limitations on collection frequency. Collective governance arrangements provide scale, standardization, and coordination, yet also create distance between financing actors and daily operations. Monitoring remains constrained by fragmented information systems, limited traceability, and unresolved questions of data legitimacy. We argue that agentic genomics shifts the bottleneck in computational biology from pipeline construction to validation. We examine emerging systems, including CellAtria, AutoBA, Bio-Copilot, and ClawBio, and assess their divergent architectures. We propose a tiered validation framework spanning research-grade, benchmarked, and clinical-grade analyses and argue that equity-aware design must be a systems requirement rather than an optional aspiration.
